claim: On 2025-04-10 Gateway Load Balancers added LCU reservation, to set a minimum bandwidth capacity on top of the existing automatic scaling.
question: When did Gateway Load Balancers get LCU reservation?

evidence.quote: | [Capacity Unit reservation](#doc-history) | This release adds support to set a minimum capacity for your load balancer. | April 10, 2025 |

Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) now supports Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation that allows you to proactively set a minimum bandwidth capacity for your load balancer, complementing its existing ability to auto-scale based on your traffic pattern.

claim: On 2025-11-19 Network Load Balancers added weighted target groups for the default action, for blue/green and canary deployments.
question: Since when can a Network Load Balancer split traffic across weighted target groups?

values.display: default action with weighted target groups

evidence.quote: | [Weighted target groups](#doc-history) | This release adds support for default action with weighted target groups. | November 19, 2025 |

Weighted target groups enables key use cases like Blue-Green and Canary Deployments, Application Migration, and A/B Testing by allowing you to register multiple target groups with configurable weights ranging from 0 to 999, providing precise control over traffic distribution.

note: d120. No saved page states the old value (one target group per forward action) verbatim. Current truth: elb-nlb-weighted-default-action.

claim: On 2025-11-13 Network Load Balancers added QUIC and TCP_QUIC protocols, forwarding QUIC traffic in passthrough mode.
question: When did Network Load Balancers add QUIC support?

evidence.quote: | [QUIC and TCP\_QUIC Protocol Support](#doc-history) | This release adds support for QUIC and TCP\_QUIC protocols. | November 13, 2025 |
AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) now supports QUIC protocol in passthrough mode, enabling low-latency forwarding of QUIC traffic while preserving session stickiness through QUIC Connection ID.

claim: On 2025-02-13 Network Load Balancers gained the ability to disable (remove) an Availability Zone of an existing load balancer; before, you could add Availability Zones but not remove them.

evidence.quote: | [Disable Availability Zones](#doc-history) | This releases adds support to disable an Availability Zone for an existing load balancer. | February 13, 2025 |
Prior to this launch, customers could add AZs to an existing NLB, but could not remove AZs.

changed.was: customers could add AZs to an existing NLB, but could not remove AZs

claim: Network Load Balancer listener rules, which route by source IP address type on a dual-stack load balancer, appear in the NLB document history on 2026-07-10 and were announced on 2026-07-22; before, serving IPv4 and IPv6 clients with their own client IPs needed two load balancers or protocol translation.
question: What did Network Load Balancer listener rules change in July 2026, and is it examinable?

values.display: route connections to different target groups
either run two separate load balancers

evidence.quote: | [Listener rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html) | This release adds support for listener rules on Network Load Balancers, enabling custom traffic routing based on source IP address type. You can route IPv4 and IPv6 traffic to separate target groups using a single dual-stack load balancer. | July 10, 2026 |

Previously, serving both IPv4 and IPv6 clients from one NLB meant accepting a tradeoff: either run two separate load balancers (one per IP version) and split clients with DNS, or send all traffic to one target group and lose the original client IP through protocol translation.
Network Load Balancer (NLB) now supports listener rules allowing you to route connections to different target groups based on the source IP address type.

changed.was: either run two separate load balancers (one per IP version) and split clients with DNS, or send all traffic to one target group and lose the original client IP through protocol translation

note: d121. Not examinable yet: general availability announced 2026-07-22, after the 2026-07-15 cutoff (history row 2026-07-10). Current truth: elb-nlb-listener-rules-dual-stack-source-ip-type.
